title: Stowaway cluster tasks and quickwins
content:
Purpose: fast personal checklist / scratchpad for the stowaway pool rebound and background cleanups. Not a runbook — just my running todo + quick commands for tonight's shift.

Context: the stowaway pool (ghost-pool-3) has been flapping after the autoscaler bump. Observed 2x spike in preemptions during the 03:00 UTC window; probably noisy neighbor scheduling + noisy GPU driver restarts on a1 nodes. Need to triage and write follow-ups.

Top priorities (order I plan to run them)
- [ ] Stabilize pool: mark suspect nodes cordoned (node tags: maybe faulty nvlink)
    - quick: kubectl get nodes -l pool=ghost-pool-3 -o wide | grep -i a1
    - quick: kubectl cordon <node> && annotate node ops/cordon-reason='noisy-driver-2025-11-02'
- [ ] Restart driver gracefully on cordoned nodes (one at a time) and watch KV cache warm-up metrics
    - command: sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver || sudo modprobe -r nvidia && sudo modprobe nvidia
    - monitor: /metrics -> gpu_kv_cache_hits, avg_token_latency_per_req
- [ ] Adjust autoscaler threshold for next 24h to reduce overreacting to transient CPU spikes (raise scale-down delay from 300s -> 600s)
    - quick config: autoscaler/ghost-pool-3 -> scaleDownDelaySeconds: 600
- [ ] Deploy small rollback of new kernel package to test lane if restarts keep failing (tag: kernel-5.19-rollback)
- [ ] Re-run nightly health-check script with verbose logging and upload logs to a temp S3 path for debugging (s3://redwood-debug/stowaway/2025-11-07)

Observations and quick notes
- Observed pattern: preemption count spikes right after model warmup calls from hosted-api experiments. Suspect shared network saturation causing kernel-level stalls -> OOM killers triggering.
- Metric snapshot (copied from grafana quick view at 02:48 UTC):
    - preemptions: 18 events / 5m (baseline 2/5m)
    - avg token latency (p95): 1.29s -> 2.7s during spikes
    - NVLINK error logs increased on a1-12 and a1-18

Hypotheses to validate (short):
- Hyp 1: kernel/drivers on a1 family are regressing under multi-tenant batching. Need to repro on staging node.
- Hyp 2: autoscaler reacts to ephemeral CPU load from hosted-api smoke tests; should debounce scaling events.
- Hyp 3: some long-running jobs are not releasing GPU memory due to older model runner; find top offenders (kubectl top/ps + nvidia-smi)

Quick commands & snippets I keep re-typing
- List suspect nodes: kubectl get nodes -l pool=ghost-pool-3 -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.status.conditions[-1].type}{"\n"}{end}'
- Find top pods by GPU memory: kubectl top pods --all-namespaces --containers | sort -k3 -nr | head -n 10
- Dump dmesg/gpu logs: journalctl -u nvidia-driver -n 500 > /tmp/nvidia-dmesg-$(date +%s).log
- Trigger staged restart on node: ssh ops@<node> 'sudo systemctl stop model-agent && sleep 8 && sudo systemctl start model-agent'

Small follow-ups / quickwins (can finish in < 30m each)
- [ ] Add a guard to the smoke-test runner so it uses smaller concurrency window when pool size < 8. (ticket: JIRA-ENGINF-1895)
- [ ] Add label 'noisy-gpu' to two nodes so autoscaler excludes them from burst allocation; short term hack.
- [ ] Create short PR to extend autoscaler cooldown and add a canary metric: scale_decision_count -> ship to dashboard.

Questions / undecided
- If we cordon two nodes and disruptions continue, do we failover to dedicated pool or throttle hosted-api experiments? Which is cheaper for a 2h window? (cost calc rough needed)
- Who should own the kernel rollback test? Ping: Maya or infra-kernels?

Notes to self for tomorrow
- Re-run repro on staging with single-tenant load, capture perf counters, check nvidia-smi persistence mode
- Draft quick incident note for #infra-ops with timeline + link to uploaded logs

Random smaller thoughts (brain-dump)
- We should track 'warmup' burst events separately in grafana (tag by route). Right now warmup traffic and genuine customer traffic are conflated.
- Consider adding a tiny caching proxy in front of kernel driver health checks to reduce probe noise.

End of scratchpad. Will convert high-priority items to tickets after shift if unresolved.

-- Rohan
